title: Pitch template part 2: insight, unfair advantage, unit economics and revenue
summary: The middle of the pitch: your insight, why others cannot copy you, business unit economics per transaction, and revenue streams as strategies.

chunks.heading: Insight and Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage
chunks.explanation_md:
Two slides ask what sets you apart, each as a sharp question.

**Insight: What do you understand that others just don't know?**

**Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage: Why it would be hard for others to duplicate what you are going to do?**

Keep the two apart: the **insight** slide is about what you **understand** that others don't know; the **unfair advantage** slide is about why others would find it **hard to duplicate** what you do.

Why it would be hard for others to duplicate what you are going to do.

chunks.heading: Business unit economics
chunks.explanation_md:
The **Business Unit Economics** slide asks for two averages:

- **Cost per transaction (Average)**
- **Revenue per transaction (Average)**

Both are measured **per transaction** and as an **average**, so you put your cost and your revenue for one typical transaction side by side.

key_terms.meaning: Cost per transaction (Average) and Revenue per transaction (Average).

chunks.exam_line: Business unit economics: average cost per transaction and average revenue per transaction.

questions.stem: Differentiate between the Insight slide and the Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage slide of the pitch template.
questions.model_answer_md:
Both slides show what sets the startup apart, but they ask different questions.

| Basis | Insight | Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage |
|---|---|---|
| Question | What do you understand that others just don't know? | Why would it be hard for others to duplicate what you are going to do? |
| About | Your understanding | Your protection from copying |
| Looks at | What you know | What others cannot easily do |

An insight can be known by you alone today; an unfair advantage keeps others from copying you even once they know.

So insight is about knowing, and unfair advantage is about being hard to duplicate.

rubric.point: Insight: what you understand that others don't know
Unfair advantage: hard for others to duplicate
Knowing versus protection from copying

questions.stem: Explain the Business Unit Economics slide of the pitch template.
questions.model_answer_md:
The Business Unit Economics slide asks the team to show the money in one typical transaction.

- **Cost per transaction (Average):** what one transaction costs you on average.
- **Revenue per transaction (Average):** what one transaction brings in on average.
- Putting the two side by side shows whether each transaction makes or loses money.

So unit economics is judged one transaction at a time, using averages.

rubric.point: Cost per transaction (average)
Revenue per transaction (average)
Side by side for one transaction

questions.stem: How does the pitch template ask a startup to show why it will win and how it will make money? Explain the Insight, Unfair Advantage, Business Unit Economics and Revenue Streams slides.
questions.model_answer_md:
After problem, solution and market, the template turns to two questions: why this startup will win, and how it will make money.

**Why it will win**

**1. Insight:** *What do you understand that others just don't know?* The team shows an understanding that others lack.

**2. Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage:** *Why it would be hard for others to duplicate what you are going to do?* The team shows what protects it from copying.

The two differ: insight is what you **understand**; unfair advantage is why others find it **hard to duplicate**.

**How it will make money**

**3. Business Unit Economics:** two averages side by side.
- **Cost per transaction (Average)**
- **Revenue per transaction (Average)**

**4. Revenue Streams:** *how you intend to make money*.
- Add **strategies, not revenue projections**, such as **pay-per-use, subscription, licensing**.
- Then complete: **we will begin commercial sales** ..., **total five year revenue estimate** ..., **at a cost of** ....

**Summary table**
| Slide | Question |
|---|---|
| Insight | What do we know that others don't? |
| Unfair Advantage | Why can't others copy us? |
| Unit Economics | Does one transaction pay? |
| Revenue Streams | How will we earn, from when, and at what cost? |

In short, these four slides prove the startup is different and that it can earn money transaction by transaction.

rubric.point: Insight: what you understand that others don't know
Unfair advantage: hard to duplicate
Unit economics: average cost and revenue per transaction
Revenue streams: strategies not projections; pay-per-use, subscription, licensing
Commercial sales start, five year estimate, cost

questions.stem: Your team runs the "Zero-to-One" Skill Academy from the list of business ideas. Fill in the Insight, Business Unit Economics and Revenue Streams slides of the pitch template using only what the handout says.
questions.model_answer_md:
The pitch template gives the slides; the business ideas handout gives the Skill Academy's content.

**Insight (what do you understand that others just don't know?)**
Students are often **deficit in the practical skills that secure internships and placements**, skills they should possess or actively perfect.

**Uniqueness / Unfair Advantage**
The handout does not name one directly. The closest point is reach: the academy fills seats through **campus networks, social media and scarcity tactics**.

**Business Unit Economics**
- **Cost per transaction (Average):** the cost of one student in a bootcamp. The handout's lesson is to calculate your **exact cost per student vs venue/software costs**.
- **Revenue per transaction (Average):** what one student pays for a bootcamp.
- Comparing the two helps **optimize margins**.

**Revenue Streams (strategies, not projections)**
- The academy earns from **high-intensity weekend bootcamps** on high-demand skills.
- Of the slide's example strategies, charging per bootcamp is closest to **pay-per-use**.
- **Product-Market Fit** guides which topics to sell: test which ones get students to **pull out their wallets**.
- The five year estimate and cost lines would be filled from the team's own numbers.

In short, the handout's problem becomes the insight, cost per student becomes the unit economics, and paid bootcamps become the revenue strategy.

rubric.point: Insight: students lack practical skills for internships and placements
Unit economics: cost per student vs venue/software costs
Template: average cost and revenue per transaction
Revenue strategy from bootcamps, linked to pay-per-use
Product-market fit guides topics
